### Q28. A patient with a weak hemiplegic arm is being transferred. Which action protects the shoulder?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Lift the patient by the affected wrist
- **B.** Allow the arm to hang without support during transfer
- **C.** Force the shoulder through resistance
- **D.** Support the affected arm and avoid pulling on it

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Support the affected arm and avoid pulling on it**

Stroke ke baad weak ya flaccid arm mein shoulder stabilizing muscle activity kam ho sakti hai. Unsupported arm ke weight se joint traction aur pain ho sakte hain. Transfer mein affected arm support karein aur trained technique use karein.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Affected wrist se lift karna force shoulder tak transmit karta hai aur pain ya injury cause kar sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Arm ko unsupported hang karne se weak shoulder par gravitational traction badh sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Resistance ke against forced movement soft tissue damage kar sakti hai. Therapist-guided range aur scapular movement ka dhyan rakhein.
- **D (Sahi):** Affected arm support karke pulling avoid karne se shoulder traction aur soft-tissue injury ka risk kam hota hai.

**Exam clue:** Hemiplegic shoulder = support, never pull on affected arm.

**Clinical reference:** [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/2-shoulder-pain-and-complex-regional-pain-syndrome)

### Q31. Which positioning principle helps prevent foot drop during prolonged bed rest?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Keep the ankles plantarflexed continuously
- **B.** Avoid inspecting the heels
- **C.** Maintain neutral ankle alignment using appropriate support and reassess the skin
- **D.** Place heavy bedding directly against the toes

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Maintain neutral ankle alignment using appropriate support and reassess the skin**

Prolonged bed rest mein ankle plantarflexed rehne se soft tissue shortening aur contracture develop ho sakti hai. Neutral alignment ko suitable support se maintain karein. Foot drop neurological weakness se bhi ho sakta hai, isliye support alone treatment nahi hai. Heel offloading aur skin checks zaroori hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Continuous plantarflexion Achilles-calf shortening aur ankle contracture ka risk badhata hai.
- **B (Galat):** Heel inspection avoid karne se pressure damage early identify nahi hoga.
- **C (Sahi):** Neutral ankle support prolonged plantarflexion ko limit karta hai. Skin, circulation aur comfort reassessment se device-related pressure harm avoid karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Heavy bedding toes par force daal kar plantarflexion aur pressure injury badha sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Neutral ankle alignment + skin checks, no prolonged plantarflexion.

**Clinical reference:** [OpenStax positioning](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-4-positioning-in-bed) · [OpenStax mobility assessment](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-2-assessing-mobility)

</details>

### Q49. Which intervention helps reduce deconditioning during a prolonged hospital stay?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Avoiding all active movement after admission
- **B.** Routine strict bed rest for every patient
- **C.** Early individualized mobilization when clinically safe
- **D.** Keeping the patient in one position throughout the day

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Early individualized mobilization when clinically safe**

Deconditioning prolonged inactivity se muscle strength, endurance aur function kam hone ko kehte hain. Clinically safe individualized mobilization se function maintain karne mein madad milti hai. Vitals, weight-bearing orders aur fall risk check karke gradual activity badhayein.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Sab active movement avoid karne se strength aur joint function deteriorate ho sakte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Har patient ko strict bed rest dena unnecessary muscle loss aur complications badha sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Early individualized activity jab safe ho, strength, functional independence aur endurance support karti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Ek position mein din bhar rehne se pressure injury aur functional decline ka risk badhta hai.

**Exam clue:** Safe early mobility, not universal bed rest.

**Clinical reference:** [OpenStax mobility assessment](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-2-assessing-mobility) · [OpenStax transfer and aids](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-3-transferring-patients)

</details>

### Q117. During first ambulation after surgery a patient becomes pale and dizzy. Which action is safest?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Encourage rapid walking to improve circulation
- **B.** Assist the patient to a safe sitting or lying position and assess vital signs
- **C.** Insist on completing the walking distance
- **D.** Leave the patient standing while obtaining equipment

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Assist the patient to a safe sitting or lying position and assess vital signs**

First postoperative ambulation mein pallor aur dizziness postural BP drop, blood loss, medication effect ya doosre cause se ho sakti hai. Walking stop karein, patient ko supported sitting ya lying position mein safely assist karein, vitals aur symptoms assess karein aur persistent ya severe abnormality escalate karein.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Rapid walking cause resolve nahi karti aur instability worsen kar sakti hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Safe sitting/lying fall prevent karti hai aur BP, pulse, oxygenation aur clinical condition check karne ka mauka deti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Distance complete karna safety se important nahi hai. Symptoms ke baad activity continue karna unsafe hai.
- **D (Galat):** Patient ko unsupported standing chhodne se fall aur injury ka immediate risk hai.

**Exam clue:** Dizzy during ambulation = stop, support, assess.

**Clinical reference:** [OpenStax transfer and aids](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-3-transferring-patients) · [OpenStax mobility assessment](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-2-assessing-mobility)

</details>

## Mock 05

### Q26. A patient slides repeatedly down a raised bed. Which tissue-damaging force is especially relevant?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Osmosis
- **B.** Shear
- **C.** Radiation
- **D.** Active transport

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Shear**

Shear mein tissue layers ek doosre ke relative shift hoti hain. Raised bed se patient slide kare to skin surface bedding ke saath resist kar sakti hai jab deeper structures move karte hain. Blood vessels distort aur tissue damage ho sakta hai. Friction-reducing repositioning aid aur clinically appropriate bed elevation use karein. Breathing ya aspiration indication ko ignore nahi karein.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Osmosis semipermeable membrane ke across water movement hai. Yeh mechanical sliding force nahi hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Shear deeper tissue aur surface ke relative movement se hoti hai. Sacral pressure ke saath tissue injury risk badh sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Radiation heat transfer ka mechanism hai. Raised bed se sliding mein specific force shear hai.
- **D (Galat):** Active transport cellular energy-dependent substance movement hai. Bed sliding se tissue layers ki mechanical distortion ko explain nahi karta.

**Exam clue:** Sliding down raised bed = shear. Friction surface rubbing hai.

**Clinical reference:** [International pressure injury guideline](https://www.internationalguideline.com/repositioning)

**MCQ practice lead (topic-level, description indexed only):** [VS Nursing Academy — Patient Safety and Positioning MCQ Sessions, Ritika Mam](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SISfTMUsLHg). Exact question and playback not verified.

</details>

### Q62. Which bed position raises the head while keeping the bed surface angled with the head higher than the feet?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Reverse Trendelenburg
- **B.** Sims
- **C.** Trendelenburg
- **D.** Lithotomy

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Reverse Trendelenburg**

Reverse Trendelenburg mein entire bed tilted hota hai aur head feet se higher hota hai. Fowler mein mainly head section elevate hota hai, hip flexion bhi ho sakti hai. Indication, BP aur sliding risk assess karein.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Reverse Trendelenburg mein bed surface head-up tilt hoti hai. Yeh stem ki exact definition hai.
- **B (Galat):** Sims lateral-semi-prone body position hai, head-up whole-bed tilt nahi.
- **C (Galat):** Trendelenburg mein head feet se lower hota hai. Yeh opposite direction hai.
- **D (Galat):** Lithotomy mein legs supported aur hips-knees flexed rehte hain. Yeh whole-bed tilt nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Reverse Trendelenburg = whole bed head-up.

**Clinical reference:** [OpenStax positioning](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-4-positioning-in-bed)

**MCQ practice lead (topic-level, description indexed only):** [VS Nursing Academy — Patient Safety and Positioning MCQ Sessions, Ritika Mam](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SISfTMUsLHg). Exact question and playback not verified.

</details>

### Q102. Which equipment is appropriate for reducing friction during repositioning of a dependent patient?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** A suitable slide sheet or transfer aid
- **B.** Pulling the patient by the elbows
- **C.** Dragging directly across rough linen
- **D.** Using a loose pillowcase as an unassessed lifting sling

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. A suitable slide sheet or transfer aid**

Slide sheet ya approved transfer aid dependent patient ki repositioning mein friction aur manual force kam karne ke liye use hota hai. Patient size, equipment capacity, staff assistance aur lines check karein. Manufacturer instructions aur facility protocol follow karein.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Approved slide sheet friction reduce karta hai aur controlled repositioning mein help karta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Elbows se pulling joint aur skin injury kar sakti hai aur controlled full-body support nahi deti.
- **C (Galat):** Rough linen par direct dragging friction aur skin trauma badhata hai.
- **D (Galat):** Unassessed pillowcase lifting sling ke roop mein load-rated nahi hota. Tear ya fall ka risk hai.

**Exam clue:** Approved slide aid, not dragging or improvised sling.

**Clinical reference:** [OSHA safe patient handling](https://www.osha.gov/healthcare/safe-patient-handling) · [International pressure injury guideline](https://www.internationalguideline.com/repositioning)

**Dedicated MCQ video:** specific verified question mapping pending.

</details>

### Q113. A patient has a new restriction against hip flexion beyond the prescribed limit. Which nursing approach is appropriate during toileting?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Ignore the restriction if the patient reports no pain
- **B.** Flex the hip forcefully to improve range
- **C.** Use suitable equipment and transfer technique that respects the specific restriction
- **D.** Use a very low toilet seat regardless of the restriction

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Use suitable equipment and transfer technique that respects the specific restriction**

Hip flexion restriction surgeon ke specific procedure aur patient plan par depend karti hai. Toileting ke liye assessed raised seat, commode ya assistance prescribed range maintain kar sakte hain. Har hip replacement patient ko same precaution ya fixed angle mandatory nahi hota.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Pain absent hona restriction safe to break hone ka proof nahi hai.
- **B (Galat):** Forceful flexion prescribed protection ko violate karti hai aur pain, tissue injury ya dislocation risk badha sakti hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Suitable equipment aur individualized transfer technique prescribed restriction maintain karte hain aur safe toileting support karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Very low seat se sit-to-stand ke waqt hip flexion badh sakti hai aur prescribed limit violate ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Specific prescribed hip limit > generic rules.

**Clinical reference:** [NHS individualized hip precautions](https://www.guysandstthomas.nhs.uk/health-information/precautions-after-hip-surgery)

**Dedicated MCQ video:** specific verified question mapping pending.

</details>

## Existing reported adaptation

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Previous-Year-Questions/Nursing-Foundations-HPSSC-HPRCA-Reported-PYQs.md` (blob `81ac7cb3cc2ae1f4627b806c434c45b8850d1de2`).

### PYQ2. Which position is commonly used for gynecological examination when both legs are supported?

**Reported exam:** HPSSC Staff Nurse 2021, Series A, Q2

[Question source](https://hpgeneralstudies.com/solved-paper-hp-staff-nurse-exam-2021-part-1-hpssc-hamirpur/)

- **A.** Prone
- **B.** High Fowler
- **C.** Trendelenburg alone
- **D.** Lithotomy

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Lithotomy**

Lithotomy position mein patient peeth ke bal leti hai. Hips aur knees flexed rehte hain aur dono legs appropriate support par rakhi jaati hain. Isse pelvic aur perineal area examination ke liye accessible ho jaata hai. Nurse privacy, consent, safe leg support aur pressure ya nerve injury ke risk ka dhyan rakhti hai. Har gynecological procedure ke liye lithotomy zaroori nahi hoti. Patient ki condition aur procedure ke hisaab se position select hoti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Prone mein patient pet ke bal leti hai. Dono legs supported rakhkar pelvic examination ka described access is position se nahi milta.
- **B (Galat):** High Fowler mein patient ka upper body upright hota hai. Yeh breathing support ke liye useful ho sakti hai, lekin stirrups wali pelvic examination position nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Trendelenburg mein poora bed head-down tilt hota hai. Yeh apne aap mein lithotomy ki leg support aur pelvic access wali position nahi hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Lithotomy mein hips aur knees flexed aur legs supported rehti hain. Isse pelvic examination ke liye suitable access milta hai.

**Exam clue:** Pelvic examination with both legs supported = lithotomy.

**Clinical reference:** [OpenStax positioning](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/9-4-positioning-in-bed).

**Historical evidence:** The existing HP General Studies report was directly retrieved. Series A, post code 892, Q2 includes lithotomy as source option 1. This independently worded adaptation has lithotomy as option D. Official original booklet and key were not authenticated. The source question asks more broadly about gynecological procedures, so the adaptation is narrower and clinically safer.

**YouTube MCQ practice:** [VS Nursing Academy — Patient Safety and Positioning MCQ Sessions, Ritika Mam](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SISfTMUsLHg). Indexed publisher description confirms positioning MCQs broadly. Lithotomy-specific coverage and exact playback are pending.
</details>
